papers.title: Differential formation of nitrate-responsive mycobacterial intracytoplasmic membranes during Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
papers.summary: Using cryo-electron tomography, this study shows Mycobacterium tuberculosis forms nitrate-induced intracytoplasmic membranes (MIMs) both outside and inside host cells in a strain-dependent manner. MIM formation during macrophage infection correlated with muted inflammatory responses, linking internal membrane architecture to metabolic adaptation within the intracellular niche.

papers.title: Distinct mechanical regulation of PFK1 isoforms during cytoskeletal remodeling.
papers.summary: Shear stress activates phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK1) and promotes its F-actin association, enhancing cytoskeletal reinforcement, glucose uptake, and ATP generation. Only the muscle isoform PFKM is essential, and its C-terminal tail is required for actin engagement — establishing PFKM as a mechanosensitive metabolic enzyme linking cytoskeletal mechanics to energy production.

papers.title: Dysfunction of caveolae in muscle disease: A cell biological perspective.
papers.summary: This review covers the cell biology of caveolae disruption in skeletal muscle disease, including caveolinopathies and rippling muscle disease. It examines how loss of sarcolemmal caveolae impairs mechanoprotection, signal transduction, nanoscale lipid organization, and T-tubule biogenesis, and proposes a unifying classification system for disease-associated caveolin-3 variants.

papers.title: Spatially ordered zygotic genome activation fulfills embryo quality control.
papers.summary: Spatially inverting the cell-size pattern of blastula embryos flipped the spatial pattern of zygotic genome activation (ZGA). Mispatterned ZGA along the animal-vegetal axis triggered embryo apoptosis via a nonautonomous anti-apoptotic signal, revealing a built-in quality-control system that surveils the spatial and temporal ordering of genome activation.

papers.title: Ceramide transfer protein regulates G-protein-coupled phospholipase signalling in photoreceptors.
papers.summary: Loss of Drosophila ceramide transfer protein (dCERT) elevated short-chain ceramides in photoreceptors and reduced the electrical response to light. Mutants showed slowed PIP2 resynthesis after PLC stimulation, with reduced ER–plasma membrane contact-site density and impaired rdgb function — implicating CERT in G-protein-coupled phospholipase signalling in vivo.

papers.title: Myosin1D directs circumferential F-actin flow to define cell chirality.
papers.summary: In Drosophila macrophages, Myosin1D and Myosin1C direct clockwise and counterclockwise circumferential F-actin flows, respectively, collaborating with Myosin2. In vitro, Myo1D self-organized a clockwise-rotating F-actin ring with aligned polarity, providing a molecular basis for how molecular motors generate cell and organ chirality.

papers.title: Cell cycle-dependent translation-mediated turnover of the long noncoding RNA Malat1.
papers.summary: Upon mitotic exit, the metastasis-promoting lncRNA Malat1 relocates to the cytoplasm and is degraded in early G1 via a translation- and SMG1-dependent pathway, resetting its abundance each cell cycle. Blocking this reset causes Malat1 accumulation, suggesting cancer-cell dormancy underlies widespread Malat1 overexpression in tumors.

papers.title: Integrins and tetraspanins mediate CD36-actin coupling and regulate CD36 organization and signaling.
papers.summary: The receptor CD36 couples to cortical actin through β1-integrin and tetraspanins (CD9, CD81, CD151). A G12V mutation in CD36's transmembrane domain disrupts its surface organization, weakens actin coupling, and abolishes thrombospondin-1-induced Fyn signaling — identifying integrin–tetraspanin complexes as a potentially ubiquitous membrane–actin coupling mechanism.

papers.title: The UPR drives gametogenesis via an unexpected response, coordinating translation and ER structure.
papers.summary: The endogenous unfolded protein response preceding meiosis in budding yeast is required for gamete production yet induces few canonical UPR targets. Its function is replaced by increased ER chaperones, reduced translation, or impaired ER protein translocation, and its absence compromises ER integrity — a physiological UPR enabling a cell-fate decision.

papers.title: Perturbation of nuclear proteins by optogenetic trapping in Drosophila ovary.
papers.summary: NLS-LARIAT, an optogenetic trapping tool fusing a nuclear localization sequence to LARIAT, induces light-dependent clustering of GFP-tagged nuclear proteins in Drosophila ovarian cells. Clustering SLBO and LSD1 phenocopied genetic inhibition and revealed rapid SLBO roles during border cell migration; nuclear envelope and chromatin structures are also targetable.

papers.title: Terno, a cyclin-interacting protein regulating meiotic exit and sperm differentiation in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Terno (teo) mutants undergo normal meiosis I and II, but spermatids undergo an extra division without prior DNA replication and show defective sperm individualization. TEO interacts with cyclins A/B and APC/C components; elevated cyclin levels drive the phenotype, and cyclin downregulation rescues it.

papers.title: Esc1-mediated anchoring regulates telomere clustering in response to metabolic changes.
papers.summary: Budding yeast telomere hyperclustering in quiescent cells results from loss of anchoring, not altered telomere–telomere interactions. Two redundant anchoring pathways act in rich medium: a PKA-dependent route inactivated by glucose depletion, and Esc1 dephosphorylation during quiescence entry; losing both releases telomeres, enabling hypercluster formation.

papers.title: Characterizing the membrane recruitment domain of BDCPs and its role in gray platelet syndrome.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM of full-length NBEAL2 reveals an N-terminal arch-like structure with C-terminal globular domains. The N-terminal α-solenoid/concanavalin A-like assembly of BEACH domain proteins functions as a modular membrane recruitment domain, and Gray platelet syndrome mutations L388P and E643V disrupt NBEAL2 membrane targeting — a structure–function disease mechanism.

papers.title: Super-resolution imaging reveals altered actin architecture at CAR-T cell immune synapses.
papers.summary: Using STED super-resolution microscopy, CAR-T cells formed structurally distinct immune synapses with reduced actin-depleted regions, fewer actin foci, and persistent microvilli-like protrusions — signs of incomplete cytoskeletal contraction and partial synapse maturation versus TCR signaling, with implications for CAR-T engineering and control of dysregulated or off-target responses.

papers.title: Ana1/Cep295 regulates centriole elongation via Cep135 and microtubules.
papers.summary: Ana1/Cep295 regulates centriole elongation in fly spermatocytes via two mechanisms: direct Cep135 interaction promoting elongation and recruitment into the proximal centriole-like structure, plus microtubule binding and bundling required in vivo. Both non-exclusive activities contribute to centriole overelongation during spermatogenesis.

papers.title: Dimerization of human PARP15 is required for NAD(+) binding and automodification.
papers.summary: Full-length human PARP15 isoform 1 auto-ADP-ribosylates on glutamate and aspartate residues within its tandem macrodomain region, reversibly by known ADP-ribosylhydrolases. Dimerization is required for efficient NAD+ substrate binding, confirmed structurally by a co-crystal of the catalytic domain dimer with an unhydrolyzable substrate analog.

papers.title: Identification of genes encoding GRF transcription factors in Taraxacum kok-saghyz Rodin and their potential role in response to salt stress.
papers.summary: Ten TkGRF genes were identified in Taraxacum kok-saghyz (Russian dandelion), all containing QLQ and WRC domains. Salt stress induced TkGRF1 most robustly; overexpression in Arabidopsis elevated MDA and ROS while reducing antioxidant enzyme activity, defining TkGRF1 as a negative salt-tolerance regulator and molecular breeding target.

papers.title: Epigenetic maintenance of PRC2-repressed chromatin requires RTT109 but not H3K56 acetylation.
papers.summary: In Neurospora, the histone acetyltransferase RTT109 is required to maintain PRC2-repressed chromatin. H3K27me3 propagates through multiple mitoses without sequence-specific PRC2 targeting, and RTT109 catalytic activity — independent of NAF-2 and H3K56 acetylation — is essential for maintenance, uncovering a replication-linked epigenetic memory mechanism.

papers.title: Genetic architecture of basal heart rate and its modulation by dietary salt in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: Using the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel, basal heart rate showed moderate heritability, significant genotype-by-environment interaction, and sex-specific genetic architectures. Salt stress unlocked cryptic genetic variation, with GWAS candidate genes confirmed by heart-specific RNAi — demonstrating environment-dependent genetic control of cardiac function.

papers.title: Galloyl-RGD induces oxidative stress-mediated apoptosis in human melanoma cells.
papers.summary: Galloyl-RGD, a gallic acid–RGD conjugate, reduced SK-MEL-28 melanoma cell viability dose- and time-dependently, inducing apoptosis, G1 arrest, ROS elevation, JNK/p38 MAPK activation, and suppression of cyclin D1, Akt/NF-κB, and Bcl-2 — positioning it as a candidate compound targeting stress-associated survival mechanisms in melanoma.

papers.title: Ebselen Inactivates Essential Mycoplasmopsis bovis Proteins.
papers.summary: Ebselen, prioritized from a ~2,800-compound repurposing screen, inhibits Mycoplasmopsis bovis growth by covalently modifying lactate dehydrogenase Cys124 and enolase Cys216 (plus elongation factor G), inactivating these enzymes with low micromolar IC50 values. Poorly conserved modification sites support narrow-spectrum therapy development against this agricultural pathogen.

papers.title: Omics-Scale Capture of Electrophilic Metabolites.
papers.summary: TAMOHA, an o-(trimethylammoniobutyl)-hydroxylamine probe, traps electrophilic metabolites — CoA esters, ketones, aldehydes — as stable charged derivatives for sensitive MS detection. Profiling E. coli, C. elegans, and mice revealed thousands of uncharacterized electrophiles and confirmed pathway functions, including formaldehyde production and ascaroside pheromone biosynthesis.

papers.title: Minimal Functional Scaffolds of the Streptococcus sinensis Competence-Stimulating Peptide Define the Balance between Receptor Promiscuity and Signaling Specificity.
papers.summary: Truncation and reverse alanine scanning of the Streptococcus sinensis competence-stimulating peptide identified minimal scaffolds retaining full quorum-sensing activation despite ~one-third sequence replacement. A D1A substitution converted agonists into competitive antagonists, and the most potent antagonist suppressed natural competence — defining determinants balancing receptor promiscuity and signaling specificity.

papers.title: Beyond clonality: invertons as engines of phenotypic heterogeneity in bacteria.
papers.summary: This perspective highlights invertons — reversibly invertible DNA elements flipped by invertases that toggle transcription, recode proteins, or alter specificity. Recently revealed as widespread in prokaryotes through sequencing datasets, invertons generate phenotypic heterogeneity within genetically clonal populations, challenging the assumption that clonal bacteria behave identically.

papers.title: ZC3H13-Mediated m(6)A Modification of TRIM16 Suppresses EndMT and Atherosclerosis by Destabilizing Ang2 and Inhibiting the TLR4/NLRP3 Pathway.
papers.summary: ZC3H13, reduced in atherosclerosis, stabilizes TRIM16 mRNA via m6A modification. TRIM16 ubiquitinates Ang2 (K48- and K63-linked), inhibiting TLR4/NLRP3 signaling and suppressing endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition; ZC3H13 overexpression attenuated atherosclerotic plaques in mice — nominating the ZC3H13/TRIM16/Ang2 axis as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Endosome restricted human TLR1 polymorphism highlights a role for MyD88 in Pam3CSK4 detection.
papers.summary: The common human TLR1 rs5743618 polymorphism retains TLR1 intracellularly. The derived allele signaled exclusively from endosomes, with altered IκBα degradation and NF-κB activation dependent on endosome-localized MyD88 — establishing compartment-specific TLR2/1 signaling relevant to inflammatory outcomes such as antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis.

papers.title: Characterization of the dual functions of Leishmania CK1.2 in both the parasite and the macrophage.
papers.summary: Leishmania CK1.2, an essential kinase, localized across cytoskeleton, basal body, and flagellum, with 230 parasite interactors across life stages and 64 host interactors involved in immune response, apoptosis, and purine biosynthesis. Its dual functions in parasite and host cell mark it as a target for leishmaniasis therapy.

papers.title: Thioredoxin h1-targeted proteins in European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.): Insights into metabolic control, stress response, and seed longevity.
papers.summary: Using a trapping mutant of thioredoxin h1 plus DDA proteomics, 161 target proteins were identified in European beech embryonic axes, including chaperones, calcium-binding proteins, and metabolic enzymes. Long-term storage depleted the reduced thiol pool ~2.2-fold, linking Trx h1-dependent redox maintenance to seed longevity.

papers.title: Associating Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic variants with minimum inhibitory concentrations to delamanid and pretomanid.
papers.summary: Seventeen delamanid-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates were phenotyped and sequenced: 47% showed MICs below the critical concentration, and the ddn W88* premature stop codon predominated among those above it. Results support ddn W88* and fbic W678G as delamanid/pretomanid resistance markers, plus novel variants in resistance-linked genes.

papers.title: Exploring the key genes of colorectal "adenoma-cancer" based on graph transformer.
papers.summary: A graph neural network (ChebTS) with attention pooling analyzed colorectal normal–adenoma–cancer transcriptome stages, identifying eight key genes — FN1, CLDN2, IL-33, MMP1, STC2, IGFBP7, NOX4, SFRP1 — all associated with overall survival and extracellular matrix remodeling, proposed as diagnostic biomarkers for adenoma-to-carcinoma progression.

papers.title: EffAtt-LungNet: An attention-guided EfficientNet framework for three-class lung histopathology classification.
papers.summary: EffAtt-LungNet combines an EfficientNetB3 backbone with CBAM attention for three-class lung histopathology classification, reaching 99.86% accuracy on an augmented LC25000-derived corpus. The authors caution this represents internal tile-level benchmark performance requiring independent, non-augmented, multi-centre validation before any clinical claim.

papers.title: Identification of new fucosyltransferase-8 inhibitors: An integrated biochemical, biophysical, and computational approach.
papers.summary: Screening 265 compounds identified eight cytotoxic to PC3 prostate cancer cells (IC50 2.94–75.82 µM) without harming normal fibroblasts. STD-NMR, differential scanning fluorimetry, docking, and simulations confirmed FUT8 binding, with anti-migratory activity in scratch assays — nominating compounds 1, 3, 6, and 7 as FUT8 inhibitor leads.

papers.title: CD3-CSPG4 bispecific T cell engager: A novel platform for malignant melanoma therapy.
papers.summary: A CD3-CSPG4 bispecific T-cell engager simultaneously bound CSPG4+ melanoma cells and T cells, enhancing T-cell proliferation and activation (CD25/CD69) and redirecting cytotoxic lysis in vitro. In NOD/SCID xenograft mice it suppressed tumor growth without detectable organ toxicity, providing a preclinical platform for melanoma immunotherapy.

papers.title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for bisphenol A neurotoxicity in depression pathogenesis.
papers.summary: Integrating network toxicology, docking, molecular dynamics, transcriptomic datasets, and mouse validation, this study identified 29 BPA–depression overlapping targets, with hubs INS, ESR1, SLC6A4, GRIA1, and NTRK2. BPA exposure aggravated depressive-like behaviors and downregulated all five hubs in mouse brain, delineating BPA neurotoxicity mechanisms in depression.

papers.title: EEG emotion recognition via multilevel entropy analysis: The power of entropy of entropy on phase dynamics.
papers.summary: Applying entropy-of-entropy analysis to EEG phase dynamics improved emotion recognition on the GameEmo dataset: a random forest classifier with mixed phase-entropy and EoE-phase features achieved 71.7% accuracy (AUC 0.869) versus ~59% for Shannon-based features, capturing second-order complexity fluctuations relevant to brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title: STZ‑induced sporadic Alzheimer's in rats: behavioral, histopathological, and MiRNA profiles.
papers.summary: In STZ-induced sporadic Alzheimer's rats, cognitive and locomotor decline, anxiety-related behaviors, elevated p-tau, and AD-like hippocampal degeneration appeared in acute and chronic phases. Let-7 miRNAs were unchanged while miR-107 was upregulated, correlating with behavioral changes — supporting miR-107 involvement in AD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Apigenin attenuates MASLD progression by suppressing lipogenesis and macrophage M1-like inflammatory activation: involvement of SMAD4-associated signaling.
papers.summary: Apigenin alleviated high-fat-diet MASLD in mice, suppressing the SREBP-1c/FAS/ACC lipogenic program and macrophage M1-like inflammatory activation. CETSA demonstrated cellular SMAD4 target engagement, and SMAD4 overexpression counteracted apigenin's effects — implicating SMAD4-associated signaling in coordinating its anti-lipogenic and anti-inflammatory actions.

papers.title: Dual action of baicalin against renal fibrosis in hyperuricemic nephropathy: targeting PANX1-P2Y6 signaling and gut microbiota dysbiosis.
papers.summary: Baicalin reduced serum uric acid and renal injury in hyperuricemic nephropathy mice, suppressing TGF-β1/p-SMAD3 signaling and PANX1/P2Y6 activation while ameliorating gut dysbiosis (increased Lactobacillus and Bacteroides). Docking and simulations confirmed stable target interactions, positioning baicalin against hyperuricemia-induced renal fibrosis.

papers.title: Trends in optimizing antibacterial cationic amphiphiles.
papers.summary: This review surveys antibacterial cationic amphiphiles — quaternary ammonium compounds, lipopeptides, and dendritic amphiphiles — often limited by host-cell toxicity. Tuning charge density, hydrophobicity, degradability, and selectivity improves potency; membrane insertion causes permeabilization, proton motive force dissipation, and energy homeostasis disruption as a common mechanistic framework.

papers.title: In vitro generation of regulatory T cells: A challenging tool for studying immune aging in humans.
papers.summary: Following a gold-standard protocol, in vitro generated induced Treg cells showed no age-related differences in FOXP3+ CD4+ cell generation between young and older donors. TGF-β was dispensable for both FOXP3 expression and suppressive activity, suggesting FOXP3 alone inadequately defines bona fide human iTreg cells.

papers.title: Selective elimination of quiescent cancer cells by dequalinium chloride via ROS-mediated ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Dequalinium chloride selectively killed quiescent cancer cells across hypoxia- and nutrient-limitation models, spheroids, and colorectal organoids while sparing proliferating cells and normal fibroblasts. It drove ROS accumulation beyond survival thresholds, causing lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis — highlighting redox imbalance as an actionable vulnerability of dormant tumor cells.

papers.title: Integrated genetic and epigenetic diagnosis of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing.
papers.summary: Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing simultaneously characterized D4Z4 repeat size, haplotype, methylation, and genomic structure in FSHD patients and a trio family, concordant with Southern blot, optical mapping, and bisulfite methods — enabling integrated genetic-epigenetic diagnosis and the first consensus D4Z4 sequences in Chinese FSHD patients.

papers.title: Integrated computational approaches for identifying and evaluating phytochemical inhibitors against HCV NS3/4A protease.
papers.summary: From ~1,480 IMPPAT phytocompounds, twenty were docked against wild-type and R155K/D168Y HCV NS3/4A protease. Ladanein and diosmetin bound all variants; MM/GBSA favored ladanein, with MD and free-energy landscape analyses supporting stable interactions — computationally prioritizing ladanein pending in vitro and biochemical validation.
